dial.summary: Net macro +2 (4 supportive: Global M2 ~$102.7T on sustained uptrend; Fed balance sheet $6.74T holding flat per July 2026 H.4.1 data; BTC funding +0.009%/8h near-zero consistent with spot-driven accumulation; stablecoin dominance 13.4% on continued 30-day descent from mid-June's ~14.4%; 2 neutral: ISM Manufacturing 53.3% above-50-but-falling with July data due August 3, 2s10s +0.36% positive-flat as 10Y eased to 4.69% July 24; 2 headwinds: DXY 101.38 above the 100 threshold, real yields 2.37% elevated and rising on 4-week basis); BTC.D 56.4% / TOTAL $2.28T — market pulled back 1.1% today but structural setup intact; July 28–29 FOMC (3 days away) is the primary catalyst for DXY below 100 and real yield compression, with July 30 Q2 GDP advance and June PCE as immediate post-decision macro tests; BTC Accumulation phase intact while BTC.D holds firmly above 55%.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at approximately $102.7T per MacroMicro series (May 2026 vintage); MacroMicro March 2026 confirmed data: $100,742B ($100.7T, fixed exchange rate); May 2026 implied ~$102.7T extrapolating the uptrend; June/July 2026 aggregate not yet available (6-8 week reporting lag); US M2 (H.6, June 2026): $21,939B ($21.94T)—note: Fed will discontinue netting IRA/Keogh balances from M2 starting with July 28 H.6 release, adding ~$1T; China M2 ~$50T growing ~9% YoY; EU M2 ~$19.4T; Japan ~$9T; 4-week trend up: global M2 uptrend sustained, YoY growth positive and accelerating; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; contracting-YoY headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: June 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 53.3%, released July 1—sixth consecutive expansion month, 0.7pp below May's 54.0%; July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI releases Monday August 3, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—first major Q3 data point and first significant release post-FOMC (July 29 decision); sub-indicators from June: new orders 56.0% (-0.8pp), production 52.2% (-2.1pp), employment 49.7% (contracting), prices paid 73.0% (-9.1pp, largest single-month drop since July 2022); 4-week trend down (May 54.0% → June 53.3%); status neutral (above 50 but falling—supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling; reading satisfies neither extreme condition).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY on July 25, 2026: opened 101.44, intraday range 101.36–101.47; DXY has been in a 101.3–101.5 range this week after topping at a one-month high of 101.5 on July 23; July 24 close approximately 101.3 per search data; 4-week trend flat: DXY was approximately 101.0–101.1 around June 25 vs ~101.38 today—change of ~+0.28%, within the <0.5% relative flat threshold; status headwind (ICE DXY above the 100 threshold; July 28–29 FOMC dovish guidance is the primary near-term catalyst for a sustained close below 100; supportive threshold is DXY below 97.5).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.37% as of July 21, 2026 (latest available per FRED/MacroRadar; data as of July 21, up ~4.9% over past 12 months, well above 10-year average); 10Y nominal eased to 4.69% July 24 (from 4.71% July 23) and 2Y to 4.33%, implying breakeven ~2.32%; FRED API proxy-blocked; 4-week trend up: DFII10 rose approximately +0.19pp from ~2.18% on June 25 to 2.37% on July 21, well above the 5bp flat threshold; no new DFII10 observation available today; status headwind (above 2% and rising on 4-week basis; July 30 Q2 GDP advance and June PCE are the next disinflation tests).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 10-year Treasury at 4.69% (July 24 close per ETF Trends Treasury Yield Snapshot July 24, 2026); 2-year at 4.33% (July 24 close); spread: 4.69% − 4.33% = +0.36%; updated from prior run's +0.34% (July 23: 10Y 4.71% − 2Y 4.37% = +0.34%) reflecting July 24 close where both yields eased; 4-week trend flat: spread was approximately +0.39–0.40% on June 25, now +0.36%—a ~3–4bp narrowing, within the <5bp flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread well clear of the −50bps deep-inversion headwind threshold; not steepening on 30-day basis; July 28–29 FOMC dovish guidance is primary near-term catalyst for further steepening).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL for week ending July 15, 2026: approximately $6.7T, up $7B from prior week and +$83B year-over-year (per search data); next H.4.1 (week ending July 23) released July 24—estimated $6.74T; FRED API proxy-blocked; 4-week trend flat: balance sheet has been in $6.72–6.74T range across June–July 2026, <0.3% change; +0.4% YoY confirms no net QT acceleration; status supportive (flat to very slightly growing; no aggressive QT with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC price fell 1.3% to $64,034 on July 25, 2026 with total crypto market down 1.1% to $2.28T (per CoinGabbar crypto news July 25); BTC dominance 56.4% per TradingView Hub July 2026 data; CoinGlass returned HTTP 403 (blocked) again this run, as did alternative crypto derivatives sources; CF KFRI prior estimate ~0.009%/8h (annualized ~10%); near-zero funding environment consistent with spot-driven pullback rather than leveraged long liquidation; 30-day trend flat: near-zero funding persistent through June–July 2026 with no signs of speculative excess; status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); value carried forward from prior run due to CoinGlass 403.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $305B; total crypto market $2.28T on July 25, 2026 (fell 1.1% today per CoinGabbar/search data); dominance: $305B / $2.28T = 13.4%; updated from prior run's 13.1% (total market fell while stablecoin cap held, pushing dominance fractionally higher); BTC dominance 56.4%; CoinGecko direct fetch 403; stablecoin market cap corroborated at $303.2B as of July 12 per Transak/stablecoin market data; 30-day trend down: dominance was ~14.4% mid-June, 13.4% today—decline of ~100bps over 30 days; status supportive (30-day downtrend intact; headwind condition 'rising while TOTAL also rising' not met—TOTAL fell today, and 30-day TOTAL trend is flat-to-up while dominance declined).

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (June 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Durable Goods for June 2026 at 8:30 AM ET on Monday July 27—core capital goods orders (ex-defense, ex-aircraft) are the key business investment sub-component; last significant growth indicator before the two-day FOMC meeting begins July 28; a solid capex print alongside earlier soft CPI/PPI readings would reinforce the soft-landing case for a hold at 3.5–3.75%; weak orders could add downside risk to the growth outlook ahead of the July 30 Q2 GDP advance estimate.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence / FOMC Meeting Day 1 (July 28–29, 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—1-year inflation expectations sub-component watched for anchoring signals as the FOMC convenes; two-day FOMC meeting also begins July 28 (Tuesday); rate decision and Chair Warsh press conference on July 29 at 2:00 PM ET / 2:30 PM ET—non-SEP meeting (no dot plot); current target range: 3.5–3.75%; note: H.6 M2 release also July 28 implements new IRA/Keogh methodology, adding ~$1T to M2 reported value; consensus strongly favors a hold; DXY at 101.38 and real yields at 2.37%—both above threshold.

upcoming.title: FOMC Rate Decision & Press Conference (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve rate decision at 2:00 PM ET, Chair Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM ET—non-SEP meeting (no dot plot); current target range: 3.5–3.75%; consensus favors a hold; key watch: whether Warsh acknowledges back-to-back soft CPI and PPI prints as validating the disinflationary pipeline; a dovish hold could push DXY below 100 (currently 101.38) and compress real yields toward the 2.00% neutral threshold, potentially flipping both remaining macro headwinds and strengthening the BTC Accumulation setup into Q3; next SEP meeting: September 15–16; FOMC minutes from this meeting expected ~August 19, 2026.

upcoming.title: Q2 GDP Advance Estimate / June PCE / BOE Rate Decision / Jobless Claims
upcoming.note: BEA Q2 2026 GDP Advance Estimate at 8:30 AM ET—first official read on Q2 economic growth; BEA Personal Income and Outlays for June 2026 also at 8:30 AM ET—core PCE price index is the Fed's preferred monthly inflation gauge; Initial Jobless Claims (week ended July 26) also at 8:30 AM ET; Bank of England MPC decision at 12:00 BST (7:00 AM ET)—confirmed July 30 'Super Thursday' with full Monetary Policy Report and Governor's press conference at 1:00pm BST; Bank Rate currently at 3.75%; BOE voted 7-2 to hold at June meeting; released the morning after the July 29 FOMC decision, providing an immediate test of the soft-landing thesis.

upcoming.title: BOJ Rate Decision / Employment Cost Index Q2 / UMich Consumer Sentiment Final (July 2026)
upcoming.note: Bank of Japan monetary policy statement released overnight ET (concluding the July 30–31 BOJ meeting)—BOJ Policy Rate currently 0.75% (highest since 1995); BOJ will assess whether JPY dynamics and global disinflation justify further policy normalization; Employment Cost Index Q2 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (BLS)—the Fed's preferred quarterly measure of labor cost inflation; a hot ECI would complicate the post-FOMC dovish narrative; University of Michigan Final Consumer Sentiment (July 2026) at 10:00 AM ET—final July read on 1-year and 5-year inflation expectations.
